paragraphs.text: i.e., She praised God, and said; for there is not one petition in all this holy hymn: but thanksgiving is a principal part of prayer; it is also an artificial begging.
paragraphs.anchor: And Hannah prayed, and said

paragraphs.text: Leapeth and danceth levaltoes, danceth a galliard; as did also Mary’s {Luk 1:47} for like cause; and betwixt this song and that of the holy Virgin there is a great likeness, as Peter Martyr rightly observeth.
paragraphs.anchor: My heart rejoiceth in the Lord.

paragraphs.text: My might and mirth is advanced. A metaphor from horned creatures, or, as some say, from conquerors setting up their crest.
paragraphs.anchor: My horn is exalted in the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Peninnah and her accomplices, over whom now I can crow and triumph, my mouth magnifically praising the Lord.
paragraphs.anchor: My mouth is enlarged over mine enemies.

paragraphs.text: "Glorious in holiness, fearful in praises, doing wonders." {Exo 15:11} This holy God is to be sanctified, {Isa 5:16} and praised; {Mat 6:9} yea, he "will be sanctified in all that draw near unto him." {Lev 10:3} The Pope, who arrogateth the title of Holiness, is injurious to God; and was no whit wronged by Philip the Fair of France, who wrote thus to him, Sciat tua maxima fatuitas, &c.: Be it known to your singular Foolishness, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: There is none holy as the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Multiply not, speak not loftiness, loftiness. Peninnah, that odious woman, had vexed and troubled holy Hannah both in her prayers and meals, with her insolent speeches. Now she is warned to have done, and not to let hard words any more to come out of her mouth, Ne lapides loquantur. See Jdg 1:15. And why? for divers good reasons: -
paragraphs.anchor: Talk no more so exceeding proudly.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Of knowledges; and he taketh cognizance of your pride and petulancy. See Mal 3:13 Mat 12:17 {See Trapp on "Mal 3:13"} {See Trapp on "Mat 12:17"}
paragraphs.anchor: For the Lord is a God of knowledge.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Exactly examined, and their {a} obliquities discovered and punished. Or, By him enterprises are established viz., if they be to his good liking, else not.
paragraphs.anchor: And by him actions are weighed

paragraphs.text: {a} The elephant, that largest of beasts, hath the smallest tongue; and nothing is said of his voice, {Job 39:1-30} to teach great men not to speak big words.
i.e., The bows of Peninnah and her children, who did shoot reproachful words at Hannah. Some gather hence that Peninnah bore no more children, but lost those she had, as 1Sa 2:5.
paragraphs.anchor: The bows of the mighty men are broken

paragraphs.text: To the same sense singeth the holy Virgin in Luk 1:46-55
paragraphs.anchor: They that stumbled.

paragraphs.text: Nimirum famelici esse, to be still hungry; they were "filled with good things," as Luk 1:53.
paragraphs.anchor: And they that were hungry ceased.

paragraphs.text: Weak for prolification; or having luctuosam faecunditatem, as Jerome saith of Laeta, who had born many children, but with this she had buried them.
paragraphs.anchor: Is waxed feeble.

paragraphs.text: He layeth men for dead, and then reviveth them, as 2Co 1:9-10. That great apostle was "in death often"; and those ancient confessors cry out, "For thy sake are we killed all the day long." {Rom 8:36} The Hebrews say that Peninnah’s children died all but two, and that those were saved alive by Hannah’s prayer for them, at their mother’s request.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord killeth, and maketh alive.

paragraphs.text: De pauperat et ditat: It is he that stoppeth that hole in the bottom of the bag, those secret drains and issues of expense, at which other men’s estates run out. {Hag 1:6}
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich.

paragraphs.text: Job, for instance; and our Henry VI, in whom it appeared that mortality was but the stage of mutability; for today he was a most potent monarch, tomorrow not the master of a mole hill. How suddenly was Joseph advanced, and David, and Daniel, and Mordecai, and Thomas Cromwell, Earl of Essex, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: He bringeth low, and lifteth up.

paragraphs.text: See Psa 75:6. {See Trapp on "Psa 75:6"}
paragraphs.anchor: He raiseth up the poor.

paragraphs.text: As he did Agathocles, Marius, Maximinus, Claudius, who, hiding himself for fear of death in a hole, was pulled out by the heels and made emperor. Michael was condemned to death by the Emperor Leo; but before the execution the emperor died, and Michael was chosen in his stead.
paragraphs.anchor: To set them among princes.

paragraphs.text: For the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s.] He hath hanged it upon nothing; only it hangeth in the midst of the heaven, equally poised with its own weight, and serveth for pillars or foundations to the whole fabric of the universe.

This is a lower love and courtesy than to keep their hands. {Joh 13:5-6} He keepeth them from utter prolapsion, from devoratory evils, as Tertullian speaketh, so as that either they fall not at all, - stumble they may, but they get ground by their stumbling, - or if they fall, they shall arise; for the Lord putteth under his hand. {Psa 37:24} There is still a supporting grace, below which they cannot possibly fall.
paragraphs.anchor: He will keep the feet of his saints.

paragraphs.text: They may fall whither they will or can, for any care God taketh of them: they shall fall and never rise again. {Zep 1:3} They have been silent in darkness, making no moan, neither humbling themselves in their distress; they "cried not when God bound them," {Job 35:12} therefore they shall be silent, sore frightened and astonished at their horrible calamities here, and tortures in hell.
paragraphs.anchor: The wicked shall be silent in darkness.

paragraphs.text: Or, Obtain his enterprise. Augustine striving against his headstrong corruptions in his own strength, heard a voice saying, In te stas, et non stas. Thou wouldst stand by thyself, and therefore fallest. See thyself weak as water, and run to Christ: rely on him alone; for God "hath laid help on One that is mighty"; he hath given "strength unto his King, and exalted the horn of his Messiah," as it is in the next verse.
paragraphs.anchor: For by strength shall no man prevail.

paragraphs.text: "As a potter’s vessel." {Psa 2:9} Turk and Pope, both those Antichrists, shall be served on this sort, saith Peter Martyr.
paragraphs.anchor: The adversaries of the Lord shall be broken to pieces.

paragraphs.text: As he did soon after this prophecy upon the Philistines. {1Sa 7:10} The mightiest men quake before God, and as the worms when it thundereth, wriggle into their holes.
paragraphs.anchor: Out of heaven shall he thunder upon them.

paragraphs.text: The Lord Christ shall; who is here first of all in Scripture called Messiah, or the Anointed One, of whom David and Solomon were types; and in that sense may also be here understood.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord shall judge the ends of the earth.

paragraphs.text: He did such offices as he was able about the tabernacle; which was the more commendable in young Samuel to be so sedulous, because Eli’s sons were at the same time so corrupt and dissolute. The word here rendered child, is by the Dutch translated Der knaben, the knave; which with them signifieth child or servant; and so it did in old English, not as now, a wicked varlet. And therefore manifest wrong is done to John Wycliffe by Bellarmine and others, because that, disallowing the invocation of saints, he called them servants, knaves, which was then a good word, - not gods, as the Papists made them.
paragraphs.anchor: And the child did minister unto the Lord.

paragraphs.text: So were Jehoshuah the high priest’s sons. {Ezr 10:18} Heroum filii noxae! Their parents, much employed about other things, are oft not so careful of well-breeding their children; and besides, they are apt to abuse their father’s authority and power to a licentious practice. Eli brought up his sons to bring down his house. He might fitly have called them, as Augustus did his lewd daughters, his ulcers or cankers.
paragraphs.anchor: Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial.

paragraphs.text: Apprehensively they knew him, but not affectively; they had no lively light, their knowledge was not accompanied with faith and fear of God. {Rom 1:21 Tit 1:16}
paragraphs.anchor: They knew not the Lord.

paragraphs.text: And the priest’s custom with the people was.] It was their custom, but not their right. Plus valet malum inolitum quam bonum insolitum. Here these priests are accused of sundry foul crimes, as ignorance, theft, sacrilege, luxury, adultery, obstinacy. A wicked priest is the worst creature upon earth. Who are devils, but they which were once angels of light?
Whether it were his part appointed him by the law or not. See Lev 7:21-22. Commonly a wanton tooth is the harbinger to luxurious wantonness. Gluttony is the gallery that lechery walketh through.
paragraphs.anchor: All that the flesh hook brought up the priest took for himself.

paragraphs.text: In that holy place, which should have struck shame into them, since it was in God’s eye, and to his face, that they committed these abominable villanies.
paragraphs.anchor: So they did in Shiloh.

paragraphs.text: Due to God by the law, {Lev 3:3-4; Lev 3:9} who well may call for the best of the best; but these liquorish Lurcos would needs be served before him, and be their own carvers. Neither waved they the breast and shoulder before the Lord, in token that they had it of his free gift: but ravenously seized upon whatsoever they liked, and said in effect, We are lords.
paragraphs.anchor: Also before they burnt the fat.

paragraphs.text: Boiled meat would not content them. But it ill becometh a servant of the Lord to be a slave to his palate. Christ biddeth his apostles when they come into a house, "eat such things as are set before them," {a} if wholesome, though but homely.
paragraphs.anchor: Give flesh to roast for the priest.

paragraphs.text: {a} τα παρατιθεμενα.
q.d., Let God have his due first; {Lev 3:3-4} but these men took no care to serve at the altar, but only to satisfy their gluttony: their gut was their god.
paragraphs.anchor: Let them not fail to burn the fat presently

paragraphs.text: The greater because they were uncounsellable, ac ne moniti quidem ab ista perversitate desistebant; but became evil examples to God’s people, who might have desired the like of them, that one did once of a bad living preacher - viz., to point him out a nearer way to heaven than that he had taught in his sermons: for he went not that way himself.
paragraphs.anchor: Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great.

paragraphs.text: Which yet was a great sin in them so to do, {1Sa 2:24} likeas it is in those now-a-days that separate from our churches because of the ill lives of some of our ministers. It is a true saying of a reverend divine, {a} The garden may be watered through a wooden gutter; the sun give comfortable light through a sluttish window; the field may be well sowed through a dirty hand; the bell call us to church, though it never enter itself but by the sound; the well may yield excellent water, though it have much mud: so may wicked ministers perform the true service of Christ, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: For men abhorred the offering of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: {a} Abbot.
He did some small charges, as setting up lights, laying up vestments, learning music, or the like. See 1Sa 2:11.
paragraphs.anchor: But Samuel ministered before the Lord.

paragraphs.text: Theoderet saith, {a} that for the excellent grace appearing in him, and the hopes conceived of him, Eli imparted unto him this honour.
paragraphs.anchor: Girded with a linen ephod.

paragraphs.text: {a} Quest. 8.
To wear under his ephod at festival times, saith Pet. Martyr, and so showed her motherly care; and did something toward his maintenance.
paragraphs.anchor: His mother made him a little coat.

paragraphs.text: In the words of God, as being his high priest: and they took it so, and sped accordingly. {1Sa 2:21} Faith is effectual.
paragraphs.anchor: And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife.

paragraphs.text: This is a periphrasis for Samuel; who being begged of God, was no less the fruit of his parents’ supplications, than of their bodies. The words may be rendered, "For the petition which he asked of the Lord": and these, saith Junius, are not the words of Eli to Elkanah, but of the author concerning Elkanah.
paragraphs.anchor: For the loan which is lent to the Lord.

paragraphs.text: In answer to Eli’s prayers for her. The like answer was returned to Dr Sandys’s prayer for his hostess, of whom taking his leave, when he departed the land for fear of Queen Mary, he said, Be of good comfort, ere that one whole year be past, God shall give you a child, a boy. And it came to pass that day twelve months, lacking one day, God gave her a fair son. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And the Lord visited Hannah.

paragraphs.text: She had five for one. So little is there lost by giving to God: he is a liberal paymaster.
paragraphs.anchor: And bare three sons and two daughters.

paragraphs.text: {a} Act. and Mon., 1894.
And with it dim sighted, and so could not see so well into the evil manners of his sons; who also haply therefore slighted him the more, because old, and overworn.
paragraphs.anchor: Now Eli was very old.

paragraphs.text: {a} That came thither for better purpose: either to be purified, as Lev 12:6, or to fast and pray, as Luk 2:37, to perform service to God in an orderly way. The Hebrew hath it, which warfared, or came together by troops, {b} as Exo 38:8, where in the LXX render the sense by the verb νηστευειν, to fast. The sin of these priests, therefore, was "exceeding sinful": for that being of a sacred calling, and wearing white ephods, they should in so sacred a place commit such villany with religious women, such as came in freely and frequently to serve God in the tabernacle: this also they did, though they had wives of their own, as being sick of a pleurisy, {Now rare or Obs.; formerly almost always in sense ‘superabundance, excess’} and like the devil, delighting to sow other men’s grounds. {Mat 13:25}
paragraphs.anchor: And how they lay with the women.

paragraphs.text: {a} Hebraei intelligunt puerperas.
{b} Turmatim conveniebant. - Jun.

This was to reprove them, Lenitate patris, non auctoritate pontificis, saith Jerome, i.e., with the lenity of a father, and not with the authority of a magistrate. This was to shave the head, which deserved cutting off, saith another. A weak dose doth but stir bad humours, and anger them, not purge them out: so it fareth with sins. Castigantur a parente Eli, leniter tamen et molli tantum brachio: Chastised these varlets {A person of a low, mean, or knavish disposition; a knave, rogue, rascal.} were by their father, but so lightly, as if he were afraid to hurt them. It is likely he had always marred them with too much indulgence: David’s fault also. Pope Paul III, hearing of the abominable practices of his son Petro Alvigi Farnesis, thought it enough to say, Haec vitia me non commonstratore didicit, He never learned these faults of his father.
paragraphs.anchor: And he said unto them, Why do ye such things?

paragraphs.text: Which Eli should have instanced and aggravated for their terror and shame. A reproof should be soundly set on. Jehoshaphat was to blame with his "Let not the king say so."
paragraphs.anchor: For I hear of your evil dealings.

paragraphs.text: Too mild all along. He should have said as Isa 57:3-4, "Draw near hither, ye sons of the sorceress, the seed of the adulterer and the whore," &c., ye degenerate brood and sons of Belial, and not of Eli; ye brats of fathomless perdition, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Nay, my sons.

paragraphs.text: He should have said, It is stark stinking naught that I hear, and woe is me that I yet live to hear it; it had been better that I had died long since, or that you had been buried alive, than thus to live and stink above ground. But he saith only, "I hear ill of you by all the people": as if he went only upon hearsay; and were put on by the people thus to check them.
paragraphs.anchor: For it is no good report that I hear.

paragraphs.text: Ye make the Lord’s people to transgress.] Or, To cry out: to transgress, even to a cry, by their abhorring the sacrifices, - see 1Sa 2:17 - which they did, but ought not to have done, - for the evil lives of those profligate priests.
The magistrate or umpire may compose the difference in such a case, and piece them together again, if they be not implacable, and if their hearts be not bigger than their suits.
paragraphs.anchor: If one man sin against another.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Directly in things concerning his service, and purposely to offend him. {Lev 15:30} Saul killed the priests to be avenged on the Lord, who had set up David.
paragraphs.anchor: But if a man sin against the Lord

paragraphs.text: Who shall be his daysman? Quid ergo si iacerdos ipse peccet? &c. What then if the priest himself, whose office is to offer sacrifice, and to intercede for others, fall into foul offences, as Cyprian {a} gravely argueth, since the means of atonement is thereby perverted and taken away? I read not in Scripture of a hypocrite’s conversion; and what wonder? for whereas after sin, conversion is left as a means to cure all other sins, what means to recover him who hath converted conversion itself into sin?
paragraphs.anchor: Who shall intreat for him?

paragraphs.text: Who should therefore have thrust them out of the priesthood, as the father of Marcion, a godly bishop, expelled him from the Church for fornication.
paragraphs.anchor: Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto the voice of their father.

paragraphs.text: God withdrew his grace from them, and gave them up to a hard heart that could not repent, that they might perish in their corruptions. This text then maketh nothing at all for the Novatians, who denied pardon to the penitent. {b} These sinners against their own souls perished by their pertinacy, or rather obstinacy in wicked practices.
paragraphs.anchor: Because the Lord would slay them.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lib. i. epist. 3.
{b} Amb., lib. i. De Paenit., cap. 8.

The worse Eli’s graceless sons were, the better Samuel was: the more amiable and acceptable both to God and men. Bad company to good people is, or ought to be, as the dirt of oysters, whose mud hath soap in it, and doth rather scour than defile.
paragraphs.anchor: And the child Samuel grew on, &c.

paragraphs.text: This was a great mercy to him, as it was afterwards to David, that "whatsoever he did pleased the people."
paragraphs.anchor: And also with men.

paragraphs.text: This man of God was Samuel, saith Junius: but that is not likely; rather it was Elkanah, as the Hebrews will have it, or some other prophet extraordinarily raised up by God, to show Eli and his sons their ingentia beneficia, flagitia, supplicia. Yet some good divines hold that this prophecy is part of that sent afterwards to Eli by Samuel, {1Sa 3:11-14} and here set down by way of anticipation.
paragraphs.anchor: And there came a man of God unto Eli.

paragraphs.text: viz., Of Aaron, of whom thou art descended by Ithamar. This referreth, saith Lyra, to Exo 4:27, before which time Aaron was a prophet, say the Hebrews, and prophesied in Egypt, reproving the Hebrews for their idolatry there, and that one of his sermons was recorded by Ezekiel. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father?

paragraphs.text: {a} Pet. Martyr.

q.d., Do ye thus requite the Lord, O ye foolish folk and unwise Qui exprobrat reposcit: God doth not upbraid any, but only in case of abuse of his benefits, which he accounts a very great indignity. Beneficium postulat officium.
paragraphs.anchor: And did I choose him? &c.

paragraphs.text: A very liberal and an honourable maintenance. {Lev 6:17 Deu 18:1}
paragraphs.anchor: All the offerings made by fire.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Why slight ye, and, as headstrong horses, {a} trample under foot my holy ordinances?
paragraphs.anchor: Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice?

paragraphs.text: “ Quae tibi pro vili, sub pedibusque iacent? ”

Choosing rather to gratify them than to glorify me, by abdicating them from the priesthood. But it may be Eli feared lest the high priesthood should by this means go from his family, as it had before from Eleazar’s for like misdemeanour, which also afterwards befell him, and he by seeking to prevent it, hastened it.
paragraphs.anchor: And honourest thy sons above me.

paragraphs.text: Whereby you intrench upon God’s part. And because Eli himself ate part thereof, he is also blamed: or rather because he suffered these disorders. Of Claudius, Emperor, it was said, Non faciendo malus, sed patiendo, fuit. And of Edward the Confessor, that, by Earl Godwin’s insolencies, though a good man, yet, not by doing, but enduring ill, he was held to be a bad prince. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: To make yourselves fat with the chiefest.

paragraphs.text: {a} Metaph. a refractario pecore. - Pisc.
{b} Dan. Hist.
Not as if God did at any time say and unsay: but many of his sayings are conditional, sc., if men reciprocate, if they prove faithful in the covenant.
paragraphs.anchor: I said indeed.

paragraphs.text: This is a bargain of God’s own making; you may bind upon it.
paragraphs.anchor: For them that honour me I will honour.

paragraphs.text: God’s visitation is like a checker board, black and white.
paragraphs.anchor: And they that despise me.

paragraphs.text: e.g., The ability and dignity of thy family. See Zec 11:17. {See Trapp on "Zec 11:17"}
paragraphs.anchor: I will cut off thine arm

paragraphs.text: Because, being an old man, thou hast no better quitted thyself in thy place and station, This was not executed for many years after, that it might be considered, and course taken to prevent it. God therefore threateneth, that he may not be put to punish.
paragraphs.anchor: There shall not be an old man in thine house

paragraphs.text: i.e., A rival, another high priest, viz., Zadok, set up by Solomon. {1Ki 1:26-27} "Thou shalt see it"; i.e., thy posterity shall, to their grief and regret:
paragraphs.anchor: And thou shalt see an enemy

paragraphs.text: In the time of Solomon’s most flourishing reign, the most gallant of that kingdom.
paragraphs.anchor: In all the wealth.

paragraphs.text: Should be so; couldst thou live so long, thou wouldst even weep thyself blind, and thy heart would fall asunder like drops of water.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall be to consume thine eyes.

paragraphs.text: One part of the threatening fulfilled shall ascertain the truth of the rest. See Zep 3:5.
paragraphs.anchor: And this shall be a sign.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Bless him with children, and settle the office firm upon them.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will build him a sure house

paragraphs.text: As Abiathar did, that officiperda, when banished to Anathoth, where he had not a maintenance. {1Ki 2:26} Let those that would shun poverty, and prevent it in posterity, take heed of snatching from others, and of pampering their paunches.
paragraphs.anchor: Shall come and crouch to him for a piece of silver.

paragraphs.text: We preach the gospel, saith an ingenuous Papist, tantum ut nos pascat et vestiat, for this end only, that we may pick a living out of it. So do too many amongst us.
paragraphs.anchor: That I may eat.
